corner_table_caption: Process, temperature and supply points simulated for the potentiostat pixel system (design point 17 of the archived Interactive.20 run: $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$). Point 1 is the typical statistical process point at \SI{37}{\celsius}; points 2--5 are the imported foundry skew corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}. Every figure and table in this section is schematic-level.

figures.caption: Potentiostat control-loop gain over five process corners, measured through the \SI{0}{\volt} probe \texttt{IPRB1} in the RE feedback path (Figure~\ref{fig:tb-pixel}). $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$, cell $R_{\mathrm{ce}} = R_u = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$, \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply. This is the full loop -- A1, A2, both feedback networks and the electrode together -- and is not the open-loop amplifier gain of Section~\ref{ss:ampab}. \texttt{tt} is at \SI{37}{\celsius}, the four skew corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}.

tables.caption: Potentiostat control-loop stability by process corner, conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:px-ctrl-loopgain}. Every corner exceeds the \SI{60}{\degree} phase-margin and \SI{60}{\decibel} DC-gain limits entered on the bench by a wide margin.

Reference-potential tracking by process corner. Cell-drive bench (Figure~\ref{fig:tb-pixel}), $v_{\mathrm{ref}}$ swept \SIrange{0}{2.5}{\volt}, $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$, cell $R_{\mathrm{ce}} = R_u = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$, \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply. Tracking error is the reference-electrode potential minus the commanded value; the worst-error row is evaluated over the fixed \SIrange{0.4}{2.1}{\volt} design-variable window (\texttt{vref\_lo}/\texttt{vref\_hi}), the same window for every corner, and is offset-inclusive. All five corners clear the \SI{1}{\milli\volt} \texttt{re\_err\_max} and \SI{50}{\milli\volt\per\volt} \texttt{re\_err\_slope} limits entered on the bench.

RE tracking range and TIA compliance range by process corner, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:px-ctrl-tracking}. Both are the width of the region over which the respective error stays inside a \SI{10}{\milli\volt} threshold; the threshold is on the total error including the loop's static offset, so a corner with more offset reports a narrower range for the same underlying loop gain -- read these next to Table~\ref{tab:px-ctrl-tracking} rather than as an independent compliance figure. The TIA range is $\pm\SI{35}{\micro\ampere}\times\SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ at the \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm} electrode used here.

Counter-electrode compliance, delivered cell current and supply current by process corner, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:px-ctrl-tracking}. Cell current is measured through the TIA feedback probe \texttt{IPRB\_F}, which carries the entire working-electrode current by KCL since no truth current is injected on this bench; both directions clear the \SI{33}{\micro\ampere} limits entered on the test by more than \SI{50}{\percent}. Supply current covers both amplifiers, both local bias generators and the shared global bias generator.

Bipolar accuracy at the $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ gain tap, the operational point at the $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ electrode, by process corner. Truth current \texttt{iwe} swept \SIrange{-36}{36}{\micro\ampere} (full scale is \SI{33}{\micro\ampere}), error referred to the nominal \SI{2.441}{\milli\volt} ADC LSB and clipped to $\pm$ full scale before taking the worst case. Over the full range the worst-case error is 0.41--0.61 LSB across corners; over the $\pm\SI{2.3}{\micro\ampere}$ subrange it improves to 0.21--0.30 LSB, the error growing toward full scale as the finite transimpedance loop gain ($\varepsilon \propto 1/T$). The converter's measured step is \SI{1.591}{\milli\volt}, not the nominal \SI{2.441}{\milli\volt} (Table~\ref{tab:adc-transfer}); multiply every LSB figure here by \num{1.535} to read it as converter codes.

potentiostat: A1 = anatop_tia_amp_ab as control amp, A2 = anatop_tia_amp_ab
as TIA, randles_cell electrode, single-ended SAR-facing output). Its `order`
places every fragment of the published section, including ones contributed by

Fragments named in `order` that do not exist are skipped silently.
SOURCE: .../tb_anatop_pixel/maestro/results/maestro/Interactive.20, points
81-85 (design point 17 of that run: PotCtrlTB + ps_iacc + ps_cv + ps_step at
rf=35k, rct_we=10k, cdl_we=100n -- the 'operational' 35k/10k pixel). Point 81
has no cor_std_mos.scs (statistical section, zero offset) so falls back to
pt81 -- hence corner_labels. Points 82-85 are ff/fs/sf/ss at 25 C; point 81 is
37 C. ps_cv/ps_step at these 5 points are NOT used here -- the Transients part
of this section sources from the separate 1M-electrode headless runs instead
(PixelCV/PixelStep configs), per the simarchive README's guidance that CV/step
should be shown at the operational max-gain (1M) electrode.
EXPRESSIONS. Every expression below is copied character-for-character from
the archived tb_anatop_pixel_iacc2/run.ocn export (the Assembler's own
ocnxlOutputExpr definitions for this bench) and independently re-verified with
OCEAN against Interactive.20 points 81-85 before this config was written.
getData(name) on the ASSEMBLER-COMPUTED output names (re_err, icell, i_fs, ...)
does NOT work here -- confirmed empirically: ?save t in ocnxlOutputExpr saves
to the ADE XL results database, not to the raw PSF, so getData("re_err")
returns nil against a real point's psf. Every expression is therefore fully
inlined from VS()/IS()/IDC() primitives, the same 'known exception' to the
'build on previously defined outputs' house style already documented in
AmpAB's _note (cross-output references are unavailable in this engine's
per-test-signal model, not merely fragile in Monte Carlo).
SIGN CONVENTION (verified 2026-08-17, firmware-critical): positive iwe flows
WE->ground; vout = V_CM + iwe*Rf; imeas = IS("/IPRB_F/PLUS") = (vout-V_CM)/rf.
ierr = imeas - iwe (measured minus true). This is the OPPOSITE sign
orientation from the simplan TB-07 formula (vcm - vout)/rf -- see
note_pixel_intro.tex.
